deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a page of raw magnetometer logs from the Gauss–Weber induction experiments of December 1834. The galvanometer circuits ran over the Göttingen wire linking the Sternwarte, the Magnetic Observatory (M.O.) and the Physikalisches Cabinet. On the previous page (Dec 16 a.m.) a bar swinging in the Sternwarte induced currents that deflected the needle in the M.O.

(A) Top of page, M.O., p.m. (1h4'30" to 1h7'0").
- Scale readings x_i are taken every 10 s, three per half-minute.
- The second column is y_i = (x_{i-1} + x_{i+1})/2. I verified this for every row. Examples: (650.4+644.6)/2 = 647.5; (644.3+646.4)/2 = 645.35; (647.8+651.6)/2 = 649.7.
- Note: 'Stand des Stabes nachdem die Verbindung mit der Sternwarte gelöst war, 1h9'0" 647.50'. This is the rest position of the needle once the circuit to the Sternwarte was opened. It serves as the zero line against which the induced deflections are measured. The smoothed values (about 645–650) scatter around it.

(B) Physicalisches Cabinet, Dec 17 1834 a.m., 11h8'44" to 11h19'39" (continued on the next page).
- Readings are taken nominally every 7 s. A few intervals are 8 s: 13'31"→39", 16'48"→56", 17'45"→53", 17'53"→18'1".
- Again y_i = (x_{i-1} + x_{i+1})/2, i.e. readings 14 s apart are averaged.
- Why this works (my explanation): write the needle's own free oscillation as A cos(ωt + φ). Then (x(t-Δ) + x(t+Δ))/2 = A cos(ωΔ) cos(ωt + φ) plus the slowly varying part, which is essentially unchanged. With Δ = 7 s, the free swing is cancelled when ωΔ = π/2. That means a full period of 28 s, i.e. a Schwingungsdauer (half period, Gauss's convention) of 14 s.
- This matches the note on the next page, 'für die Schwingung von 14" besser 13"68'.
- The slower induced motion passes through almost undiminished. For a period of 83.6 s the factor is cos(2π·7/83.6) ≈ 0.865.

(C) Header formula: 'Minim. der Induc. Schwingung bei 11h9'4".1 + 83".6·n'.
- This is a linear ephemeris for the minima of the induced oscillation, t_n = 11h9'4.1" + 83.6 n seconds.
- Checked against the smoothed column, predicted vs. observed minimum:
  - n=0: 9'4.1" vs 9'5" (498.95)
  - n=1: 10'27.7" vs 10'22"–29" (499.7/499.8)
  - n=2: 11'51.3" vs 11'53" (499.4)
  - n=3: 13'14.9" vs 13'17" (497.85)
  - n=4: 14'38.5" vs 14'42" (497.9)
  - n=5: 16'2.1" vs 16'6" (497.15)
  - n=6: 17'25.7" vs 17'24"–31" (497.35)
  - n=7: 18'49.3" vs 18'50" (498.3)
  - On the next page, n=18, 19, 20 give 34'8.9", 35'32.5", 36'56.1", matching minima near 34'14", 35'31", 36'55".
- The page thus serves to separate the needle's own 13.68 s swing from the forced induced oscillation (period 83.6 s). The epochs and amplitudes of the latter are later tabulated on the next page as a sin A against n.
errors: 16'48" row: the smoothed value 502.6 implies the reading at 16'56" is 501.0, not 501.6. With 501.0 both 502.6 = (504.2+501.0)/2 and the 17'3" value 500.6 = (501.0+500.2)/2 are exact. So the arithmetic is consistent and the transcription is at fault.

Readings written with a wrong hundreds digit (606.4, 603.7, 596.7) are contradicted by the neighbouring means. They must be 506.4, 503.7 and 496.7. These are either pen slips or misreadings of the hand; the computed means use the correct values.

Time labels: four intervals are 8 s instead of 7 s (13'31"→39", 16'48"→56", 17'45"→53", 17'53"→18'1"). They are probably genuine clock adjustments rather than errors. If the true spacing was uneven, the cancellation of the 13.68 s swing is slightly imperfect.
No genuine arithmetic errors were found in any of the roughly 110 means checked.

results.what: Smoothing a damped-oscillation record by averaging readings one Schwingungsdauer apart, y_i=(x_{i-1}+x_{i+1})/2, to remove the needle's free swing and recover the slowly varying (induced) deflection
results.modern_name: two-point moving-average / comb filter with a zero at the instrument's natural frequency
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, Göttingen magnetic method (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins, 1836ff.)

results.what: Linear ephemeris for minima of the induced oscillation, t_n = 11h9'4.1" + 83.6 n s
results.modern_name: least-squares/linear fit of oscillation epochs (period determination)
results.usually_credited_to: standard observational practice; Gauss–Weber induction experiments 1834–35

results.what: Use of the rest position after opening the circuit as the reference zero of the induced deflection

deep.surprise_reason: These are raw laboratory logs from the well-documented Gauss–Weber induction and telegraph experiments of 1834. The smoothing and period fitting are Gauss's known Göttingen observing technique. The fit of 83.6 s to the minima is a nice detail but not a new result.

checkable.asserts: First M.O. mean: (650.4+644.6)/2 = 647.5, so the result is 0
The 11h9'40" mean 504.1 requires the 9'47" reading to be 506.4 (not 606.4); result 0
The 12'42" mean is 503.65, i.e. 503.7 as written with first digit 5 (not 603.7)
The 16'48" mean 502.6 is consistent if the 16'56" reading is 501.0
The 17'3" mean 500.6 is also consistent with the 16'56" reading being 501.0

The 17'17" reading 494.7 has neighbours 500.2 and 496.7 (not 596.7). The check gives mean 498.45 = (500.2+496.7)/2; the line shown is a template and the real check is (5002/10+4967/10)/2 - 49845/100 == 0
Averaging readings ±7 s apart annihilates an oscillation of full period 28 s (Schwingungsdauer 14 s); value 0
The same smoothing passes the 83.6 s induced oscillation with factor about 0.865

transcription_corrections: Header: 'Min. m. der Induc. Schwingung bä[?]' should read 'Minim. der Induc. Schwingung bei'.
Header formula: '11h9'4"1 + 83."6[?] n' should read '11h9'4".1 + 83".6·n' (times of minima of the induced oscillation).
11h9'47": first-column value '606.4' should be 506.4 (forced by the means 504.1 and 504.1 of the neighbouring rows).
16'56": first-column value '501.6' should be 501.0 (forced by both neighbouring means, 502.6 and 500.6).
16'34": the second-column value 501.7 is written over a correction in the image (a digit is struck).
